* The fear-immunity timer is not refreshed by subsequent attempts to {{tip|fear}} the target.
** The timer remains active for a short period after the initial fear ends, allowing one ability to apply the crowd control and a subsequent ''Terrify'' to deal its doubled damage.
** When the {{tip|fear}} is applied by another ability through ''Terrify's'' passive, the fear-immunity timer lasts {{tt|{{fd|1}} seconds|Estimated}} longer.
** [[Monster#Epic monsters|Epic monsters]] are immune to the crowd control effect of {{tip|fear}}, but are still affected by the fear-immunity timer. ''Terrify'' will therefore deal doubled damage to them while the timer is active, although the damage is still limited by its 400 damage cap against monsters.
* The fear-immunity timer is applied even if the target is {{tip|cc-immune|crowd control immune}}. It is not applied if the effect is blocked by a {{tip|spell shield}}.
* The {{tip|fear}} from ''Terrify'' is applied {{tt|at the end of the cast time|0.363 seconds after the start of cast, due to game tick rate}}, regardless of the target's distance.
** Since [[V14.14|V14.14]], the missile can be destroyed by {{tip|projectile|projectile-interception}} effects.
* ''Terrify'' will still cast and affect the target even if '''Fiddlesticks''' dies or loses {{tip|sight}} of them during the cast time.
** ''Terrify'' will still cast but will not affect the target if they die, become {{tip|untargetable}}, or enter {{tip|stasis}} before the missile reaches them. Its mana cost and cooldown are not refunded.
* The meaning of "[[combat status|out of combat]]" in ''Terrify's'' description is somewhat imprecise. For the purposes of its passive, '''Fiddlesticks''' becomes eligible to fear approximately {{tt|{{fd|2.25}} seconds|Estimated}} after it has stopped dealing damage, provided it has also not taken damage from an enemy champion or been affected by crowd control during that time.
** Dealing damage to any unit counts for this purpose, including {{tip|champion|champions}}, {{tip|minion|minions}}, {{tip|monster|monsters}}, {{tip|turret|turrets}}, inhibitors, jungle plants, {{tip|ward|wards}}, and summoned units.
** Damage from item effects such as {{ii|Liandry's Torment}}, as well as [[Crest of Cinders]], [[Aspect of the Dragon]], {{si|Smite}}, and {{si|Ignite}}, also counts as dealing damage and resets the timer.
** Using {{si|Exhaust}} on an enemy champion also breaks this state despite dealing no damage. Other non-damaging summoner spells do not.
** The active slow from {{ii|Randuin's Omen}} does not break this state. Damage dealt to monsters by [[Named item effect#Jungle Companion|Jungle Companions]] also does not reset the timer.
** Damage from non-champion units does not break this state. However, crowd control from non-champion units still does, which is especially relevant when fighting {{ui|Ocean Drake}} and {{ui|Hextech Drake}}.
* Once the out-of-combat requirement is satisfied, '''Fiddlesticks''' becomes eligible to apply ''Terrify's'' passive while unseen by the enemy team, causing its other damaging abilities to additionally {{tip|fear}} affected targets. Pretending to be an {{ai|A Harmless Scarecrow|Fiddlesticks|Effigy}} can also enable the passive.
** Enemy {{tip|sight}} from any source can prevent the unseen condition from being satisfied. See [[Sight]] for further details.
* The passive portion does not normally communicate its current state to '''Fiddlesticks''', its allies, or its enemies. There is no indicator or buff icon showing that '''Fiddlesticks''' is currently eligible to apply {{tip|fear}}.
** While '''Fiddlesticks''' is channeling {{ai|Crowstorm|Fiddlesticks}}, a visual indicator will circle around enemy champions if the unseen requirement was satisfied when the channel began. This indicator is visible only to '''Fiddlesticks''', but does not guarantee that ''Crowstorm'' will apply {{tip|fear}}, as gaining enemy {{tip|sight}} or taking champion damage during the channel can invalidate the passive before ''Crowstorm'' deals damage.
** The indicator briefly appears when {{ai|Crowstorm|Fiddlesticks}} is cast even if ''Terrify'' has not been learned, but disappears almost immediately.
* There is a very brief grace period after '''Fiddlesticks''' becomes visible or enters combat during which ''Terrify's'' passive can remain active.
** This allows '''Fiddlesticks''' to move slightly out of vision-blocking terrain, such as brush, or immediately retaliate after being revealed and still apply {{tip|fear}}.
** This grace period is shorter than the cast times of '''Fiddlesticks's''' basic abilities, and therefore normally cannot be used to cast one fear-applying ability and then follow it with another.
** {{ai|Crowstorm|Fiddlesticks}} is an exception. After '''Fiddlesticks''' relocates from an unseen location into enemy vision, an ability cast immediately after arriving can still apply {{tip|fear}} before the grace period expires. This allows interactions such as ''Crowstorm'' into {{ai|Reap|Fiddlesticks}}, as well as the ''Crowstorm''–{{ai|Bountiful Harvest|Fiddlesticks}}–{{si|Flash}} interaction.
* {{si|Flash|Flashing}} into enemy vision immediately removes ''Terrify's'' passive eligibility, rather than benefiting from the normal grace period.
** This prevents most attempts to {{si|Flash}} into {{ai|Bountiful Harvest|Fiddlesticks}} or {{ai|Reap|Fiddlesticks}} from applying {{tip|fear}}, and prevents '''Fiddlesticks''' from fearing nearby enemies with {{ai|Crowstorm|Fiddlesticks}} and then {{si|Flash|Flashing}} to fear more distant enemies.
** However, if an ability that is already eligible to apply {{tip|fear}} is cast before {{si|Flash}}, that cast retains its fear effect. Combined with the brief grace period after ''Crowstorm'' completes, this is the basis of the ''Crowstorm''–''Bountiful Harvest''–''Flash'' interaction.
